name: tade_agent_harness
description: Run an agent in another harness — the program that is the agent: pi, or Claude Code on the account it is signed in to — from its next start on; a running agent is started again in it, and a conversation does not move between harnesses. Only when the human asks. Tade says which harnesses exist and which it can run yet.

harness.description: the harness id: pi or claude-code

name: tade_agent_model
description: Switch the model an agent is running on: "switch refunds to opus 5", "use kimi in agent-1". New agents start on it from then on, until another is chosen; agents already working keep their own. Say the model the way the human did; Tade finds it among the models they are signed in to, and says which it means when more than one fits. The agent must be running: to start one on a model, give the model to tade_run_start instead.

model.description: the model as the human said it: "opus 5", "claude-sonnet-5", "kimi k2.6"

name: tade_agent_rename
description: Give an agent a name: what its work is called, shown in the window and in its own session. Only when the human asks to rename it. A name they give is never replaced by one Tade would have chosen.

name.description: the new name, as they said it

name: tade_agent_thinking
description: Set how hard an agent thinks before it answers — off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max — from its next turn: "think harder on refunds", "less thinking for agent-1". New agents think that hard too, until another level is chosen. A model that cannot think that hard takes the most it can. The agent must be running.

level.description: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max

name: tade_approvals
description: Commands agents are waiting for permission to run.

name: tade_approve
description: Let a waiting command run. Only after the human has agreed to that exact command.

name: tade_deny
description: Refuse a waiting command, telling the agent why.

name: tade_done
description: Mark a task finished because the human said it is, whatever its rule: work waiting on it starts. Not for your own guess that it looks done — ask them.

summary.description: what was done, in a line, when they said

name: tade_logs
description: What has happened recently, from the journal: tool calls, approvals, failures and turns. Use it to answer questions about the past rather than guessing.

name: tade_orchestrator_model
description: Switch the model you — the orchestrator — think with: "use opus 5 yourself", "change your model to sonnet". Say the model the way the human did. It takes effect from your next reply and is kept for the next time Tade starts. For an agent's model use tade_agent_model; for "both", call each.

model.description: the model as the human said it

name: tade_park
description: Set a task aside. Nothing is lost: the worktree stays and it can be picked back up.

name: tade_plan
description: Start several changes as one plan: agents that can work at the same time start now, and the rest wait in Tade's queue until what they wait on has finished, then start by themselves. Before calling it, read the code to see what each change will touch. In a project whose agents share one checkout, never let two agents that change the same files run at once: make one wait on the other. Small changes to the same place are one agent. Give every wait a reason, and choose how each agent counts as finished. Nothing is made if the plan cannot be kept, and it says why.

said.description: the whole request, word for word

agents.description: one entry per agent, in any order

name.description: its task name, lowercase with dashes

said.description: the words of the request this agent covers, word for word

prompt.description: what to tell the agent first

done.description: how this task counts as finished, which is what work waiting on it waits for. said: its agent says it has finished (the usual choice); idle: its agent ends a turn with nothing waiting on anyone, for small jobs done in one go; committed: its agent stopped with its work committed (worktree mode only); merged: its branch is merged into the base (worktree mode only); manual: only when someone marks it finished. Anyone can also mark any task finished by hand.

after.description: what it waits on: other agents in this plan by name, or tasks already in the project

agent.description: an agent in this plan, or an existing task

why.description: why it has to wait, in a few words

touches.description: the files or folders it will change, as you read the code

at.description: not before this time, ISO 8601 with a time zone, when it should wait for one

model.description: the model to start it on, only when the human named one

thinking.description: how hard it thinks: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh

name: tade_propose_skill
description: Write down a lesson about working here — something you noticed that would have helped you earlier. It is saved as a proposal and does nothing until a human reads it and activates it. Propose one only when you have actually learned something, not to be helpful.

text.description: the lesson, in markdown, in your own words

about.description: the project or task it is about, like checkout or checkout/refunds. Leave it off only when the lesson is about working here in general: a lesson scoped to something stops being mentioned once that thing goes quiet, and an unscoped one is repeated forever.

name: tade_queue
description: What is waiting to start, and why: after what, until when, held by what, or paused. Work held because agents at work have already changed the files it was planned around says so, and says which files and whose. Answer questions about queued work with this, not from memory.

name: tade_queue_change
description: Change queued work or a schedule, as the human asked. For queued work: start it now whatever it waits on, pause or resume it, wait again past what held it, remove it, or put it in an order (change: order, with order: the tasks first to last) — an order is only a preference among work that is already ready, and never jumps a wait, unholds a hold or starts anything. Name no task to pause or resume a whole project's queue. For a schedule: start runs it now, and it can be paused, resumed, renamed or removed.

schedule.description: the schedule, by the id tade_queue lists it with

name.description: the new name, when renaming a schedule

project.description: the project, when pausing or resuming all of its queue

order.description: for order: the queued tasks, first to last; what is left out keeps its place behind

name: tade_remember
description: Write down something the human told you, in their words. Scope it to a task or project when it is about one; leave it off when it is about everything.

text.description: exactly what they said, never a tidier version of it

summary.description: a headline for it in your own words, a few words long: what it is about and what it does, like "Refunds go through the ledger". It is shown above the note in the window, so it is the line somebody reads first. It never replaces the note — write it as well as, not instead of, their words.

about.description: task or project it is about, if any

name: tade_resume
description: Pick a parked task back up, so it counts as work again.

name: tade_run_cleanup
description: Stop agents that match a state filter: idle (not actively working), done (ready to merge, in review state), failed, or all (any non-working agent). Use when the human asks to clean up finished or failed agents.

filter.description: which agents to stop: idle, done, failed, or all

name: tade_run_list
description: The agents working right now, and the task each is on. One agent per task at most.

name: tade_run_start
description: Start an agent working on an existing task. The prompt is what the agent is told first; files the human attached to what you are answering go with it. When they named a model for the work ("use opus"), pass it here so the agent starts on it: Tade finds it before anything starts, and when it cannot tell which model they meant nothing starts and it says what to ask them.

prompt.description: what to tell the agent first

model.description: the model to start it on, as the human said it: "opus", "kimi k2.6". Only when they named one.

name: tade_run_stop
description: Stop the agent working on a task. The task and its worktree stay; only the agent ends.

name: tade_schedule
description: Put work on a clock: once at a moment, or again and again — every so often, at times of day, on days of the week or month, or by cron. Each time, it starts an agent (agent: what to tell it), asks you something (ask), or looks with a watch an extension offers (watch: listed with the extension, like sentry.new-errors), which starts an agent on each new thing it finds — or tells you, with found: ask. A watch looks as often as it says unless when is given. It runs while Tade is open, and catches up once for what came due while it was closed unless told to skip. Made again under the same name, it is changed. Say back when it next runs, which this answers with.

name.description: what it is called, in a few words

said.description: what the human said, word for word

at.description: once, at this moment: ISO 8601 with a time zone

every.description: every so often, like 30m, 2h, 1d; or day, weekday, week or month with times and on

times.description: times of day, HH:MM, for day, weekday, week or month

on.description: days: mon to sun for week, 1 to 31 for month

cron.description: for anything else: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week

tz.description: an IANA time zone, like Europe/Sarajevo; the machine’s own when not said

agent.description: start an agent each time, told this

ask.description: ask you this each time, instead of starting an agent

watch.description: look with this extension's watch each time, like sentry.new-errors

input.description: what the watch is turned on with, when it takes anything

found.description: what each new thing a watch finds becomes: an agent on it, or a question for you. Left out, it is what the watch says it is for — and one with nothing to start, like an agent going in circles, only ever tells you

most.description: at most this many new things one look acts on; the rest wait for the next (2 unless said)

done.description: how this task counts as finished, which is what work waiting on it waits for. said: its agent says it has finished (the usual choice); idle: its agent ends a turn with nothing waiting on anyone, for small jobs done in one go; committed: its agent stopped with its work committed (worktree mode only); merged: its branch is merged into the base (worktree mode only); manual: only when someone marks it finished. Anyone can also mark any task finished by hand.

missed.description: what happens to runs that came due while Tade was closed: once (the default) or skip

name: tade_status
description: Where everything stands: every task, its state, and why. Derived fresh from git, running agents and provider transcripts. Use this for any question about what is happening.

name: tade_steer
description: Tell the agent working on a task something, without stopping it.

name: tade_task_create
description: Create a task: a branch, a worktree, and the human's intent recorded verbatim. Pass the intent exactly as they said it, never paraphrased. Give it the context and links you gathered, so the agent that works on it starts knowing what you know.

name.description: short task name, lowercase with dashes

intent.description: what the human said, word for word

context.description: what the agent should know before it starts, in markdown: what you found, where to look, what done looks like. Written to .tade/context.md in its worktree.

links.description: where the work came from: an issue, a trace, a discussion

done.description: how this task counts as finished, which is what work waiting on it waits for. said: its agent says it has finished (the usual choice); idle: its agent ends a turn with nothing waiting on anyone, for small jobs done in one go; committed: its agent stopped with its work committed (worktree mode only); merged: its branch is merged into the base (worktree mode only); manual: only when someone marks it finished. Anyone can also mark any task finished by hand.

name: tade_terminal_close
description: Close a terminal, ending whatever is running in it. Only when the human asked for that.

terminal.description: which terminal: its name ("tests"), its number, or its id; leave it out when there is only one

project.description: project name, as configured, when it is not obvious

name: tade_terminal_list
description: The terminals open along the bottom of the window, with their names, projects and folders.

project.description: project name, as configured, when it is not obvious

name: tade_terminal_open
description: Open a terminal: a shell in the project's folder, or in the folder given (an agent's worktree, say). It appears along the bottom of the window.

name.description: what to call it, like "tests" or "server"

cwd.description: folder to start in, when not the project itself

name: tade_terminal_read
description: What a terminal shows, with some of its scrollback: how to see what a command printed.

terminal.description: which terminal: its name ("tests"), its number, or its id; leave it out when there is only one

lines.description: how many lines back, 200 unless said

project.description: project name, as configured, when it is not obvious

name: tade_terminal_rename
description: Rename a terminal, so it can be found by what it is for: "tests", "server".

terminal.description: which terminal: its name ("tests"), its number, or its id; leave it out when there is only one

project.description: project name, as configured, when it is not obvious

name: tade_terminal_run
description: Run a command in a terminal, exactly as if the human typed it and pressed enter. They see it happen. Read the terminal afterwards to see what it printed.

terminal.description: which terminal: its name ("tests"), its number, or its id; leave it out when there is only one

submit.description: false to type it without running it

project.description: project name, as configured, when it is not obvious

name: tade_terminal_search
description: Find lines in a terminal's scrollback containing some text, any case.

terminal.description: which terminal: its name ("tests"), its number, or its id; leave it out when there is only one

project.description: project name, as configured, when it is not obvious

name: tade_updates
description: What Tade runs and whether it is current: every program it shells out to — the harnesses, the driver, git, gh — with which version is installed, how it was installed, and what to run to move it forward, plus whether there is a newer Tade. Use it when asked whether anything is out of date. `check` asks the registries, which reaches the network and takes a few seconds; without it this is only what is installed here. It installs nothing: say the command back and let the person run it, or tell them Settings › Updates has a button for it.

check.description: also ask what is current (reaches the network; a few seconds)

name: tade_write_extension
description: Write a new tool for yourself. It is saved in the extensions folder turned off, and does nothing until a human reads it and turns it on — in Extensions, or `tade extensions enable` — after which it loads the next time Tade starts. Never assume a tool you wrote is available.

source.description: the extension source: a pi extension module

why.description: what it is for, in one sentence
